maha.name: Maha
maha.description: Major cultivation season associated with the main rainy period in Sri Lanka.

notes: Chilli can be cultivated during the Maha season from late October to mid-November.
Rainfed Maha maize cultivation can be started in late September or early October.

planting_window: Nursery establishment around the end of August
notes: The source gives the end of August as one suitable period for tomato nursery establishment.
Rainfed cowpea cultivation during Maha should preferably begin around mid-November.

source.name: Department of Agriculture, Ministry of Agriculture (2016)

planting_window: Direct sowing with the first rains in October
Nursery establishment during the first week of September
Transplanting during the second or third week of October
notes: These recommendations apply to Maha-season upland finger millet cultivation.

yala.name: Yala
yala.description: Cultivation season associated with the secondary rainy period in Sri Lanka.

notes: Chilli can be cultivated during Yala from April to early May.
Yala maize cultivation can be started in early April.
The source gives mid-March as one suitable period for tomato nursery establishment.

planting_window: With the first rainfall received in April
notes: Yala cowpea cultivation should preferably begin with the first rainfall received in April.

source.name: Department of Agriculture, Ministry of Agriculture (2016)

planting_window: Nursery establishment during the first week of March
Transplanting during the first week of April
notes: These recommendations apply to Yala-season paddy cultivation of finger millet.

planting_window: Can be cultivated throughout the year under controlled conditions
Can be cultivated throughout the year in the dry zone when adequate irrigation and insect pest management are available
